# SPD-025 — Spud's Stop: a spawn allowed but never bound is invisible

## Brief
SPD-018's planned-never-spawned hold skips a planned row with an allowed spawn request still waiting to bind, as its brief says, so a spawn in flight never holds a turn. But a spawn the harness fails after PreToolUse(Agent) allowed it leaves exactly that row for ever: planned, reserved, holding a fan-out and a concurrency slot, and named by nothing unless Spud happens to retry the spawn and reads the reservation refusal. Counting a reservation that has waited more than a few minutes as never spawned would close it with the same command.

Evidence: bin/spud on branch worktree-spd-018-stop-hook-sessions: stop_owed's planned query has NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM spawn_requests s WHERE s.member_id = m.id AND s.decision = 'allow' AND s.agent_id IS NULL); hook_agent_spawn's second-spawn refusal already says 'If that spawn failed in the harness, record it with spud --as spud member finish <ref> --status failed' and is the only place such a row is ever named. No live row is in that state today (every live spawn_requests row is bound, read 2026-09-13).

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, the persona tier, no children and no probe: a harness-failed spawn cannot be produced on demand, so the tests build it from a spawn request aged past the grace. No Fable (Eric, 2026-09-13). Design decided at start: a planned row whose allowed spawn request is still unbound counts as owed once the request has waited longer than `PLANNED_GRACE_SECONDS` (ten minutes), scoped like the rest to the spawning session, with its own clause naming the reservation and the way out (look for a binding gap in `spud events --kind hook.error`; else record the row failed and plan a new one, since the reservation refuses a second spawn). Before the grace a reserved row is a spawn in flight and never holds. [[SPD-027]] changes the wording of the same hook's returned clause; this ticket leaves the existing clauses as they are. Spud reads the diff and reruns the suite at return.
